- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00 or 0.50) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase downward bias or adjust for mean reversion.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% after peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often drifts toward mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in early days of 30d window (e.g., first 5–7 days), model is often too optimistic — apply early correction: reduce first 3–5 days of forecast by 3–5%.
- If sentiment history includes alternating bullish/bearish signals, model tends to “overfit” to sentiment — dampen sentiment influence on forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.50.
